narration: Here's something nobody ever explains — to actually spend $100, you had to earn over $150 first. Let's break that down.
visual: A $100 bill SVG springs onto dark screen, question mark appears above it, then an amber badge reveals 'EARN $153' below — hooking the viewer into the math

narration: It starts the second you get paid. In the 22% federal bracket, the IRS takes 22 cents from every dollar before you even see it.
visual: Person silhouette with green income bar rising, IRS government building slides in from right, amber chunk of the bar breaks off and flies to the building on light background

narration: But that's not all. On top of that, 7.65% goes to payroll taxes — Social Security and Medicare. Most people barely even notice this one.
visual: Pay stub SVG card showing GROSS PAY, FEDERAL TAX, and FICA lines fading in sequentially, FICA row glows amber on dark background

narration: Now you've got money to spend — but the register adds one more layer. Sales tax averages 7.5% nationwide, right at checkout.
visual: Shopping bag and receipt SVG sliding up with three line items: SUBTOTAL $93, TAX (7.5%) $6.98, TOTAL $100 — tax line pulses amber on light background

narration: Add it all up. Earn $153. Federal takes $34. FICA takes $12. State takes $7. Sales tax takes $7.50. That's $60 gone and $100 to spend.
visual: Tall stacked bar chart builds bottom-to-top: green kept portion, then red federal, orange FICA, yellow state, amber sales tax — labels reveal beside each segment on dark background

narration: The fix? Pre-tax accounts. A 401k, HSA, or FSA spends money before income taxes hit — turning $100 you put in into $153 worth of buying power.
visual: Three shield icons spring in labeled 401k, HSA, FSA with dollar signs protected inside each, CTA button 'FOLLOW FOR MORE' fades in at bottom on light background
